messages:
anika: quick follow-up from the SM capability shim RFC — thinking about the runtime interface for selecting A100/H100/L4 kernel paths. want to sync on a minimal probe + fallback strategy before i land the patch.

mike_g: +1. curious about the cost of probing at request time vs once-per-worker. A100/H100 differences are mostly tensor core availability + async copy semantics.

jia: for perf we should probe at worker start and cache results. probing per-request will kill tail latency when we hit cold warps. we can re-probe if driver upgrade or env change.

ravi: agree with cached probe. also need to gate by cuda runtime version. H100 fast fp16 path depends on cuda >= 12.5 and sm80+ flags in ptx.

anika: proposal: probe sequence at startup -> read SM version, query cuDeviceGetAttribute for asyncCopy support, check driver/cuda version, then set runtime.capabilities = [H100,A100,L4] ordering. patch adds a small shim that exposes select_kernel(model_meta, capabilities)

mike_g: can we avoid expensive device queries? sample code:
```
int sm = props.major * 10 + props.minor;
bool async_copy = (props.asyncEngineCount > 0);
```
This is cheap. but we might need to inspect PTX for tensor core primitives for older drivers.
```

jia: we should also check allowed_quantization_profiles; L4 double-conversion path requires different kernel params. some profiles will be forced to A100/H100 because of numeric precision needs.

ravi: runtime-side API shape suggestion:
- runtime.probe() -> list of capability flags
- kernel_selector.select(model, seq_len, capabilities, hints) -> kernel_id
- kernel_runner.run(kernel_id, args)

keep select pure (no device interaction) so it's testable and deterministic.

anika: yes. select should be deterministic and unit-testable. i also want a small fallback table: if selected kernel missing at runtime, fallback to slower compatible kernel and emit metric REDWOOD_KERNEL_FALLBACK{from,to}.

mike_g: fallback rules need to consider register pressure. H100 kernel often uses more regs; on L4 we might need the lower-reg variant. we should include a cost model: tokens/sec estimates per kernel, and choose highest perf that fits device.

jia: cost model is tough but we can start with heuristics: prefer tensor-core kernels when fp16 and seq_len >= 64, else generic. add blacklist per model if we see quality regressions.

anika: rollout plan: land shim + probe in canary pool, enable for one model family (redwood/opt-13b) with canary config, measure latency, fallback rate, and quality diffs. deploy-bot will kick off canary.

deploy-bot: Canary started: sm-shim-v2 -> pool:eng-runtime-canary, 10% workers, tag:sm-shim-2026-03-18

ravi: small ops question: how do we surface capability flags in the console? want per-region/device dashboard and an alert if fallback rate > 1%.

anika: i'll add metrics: kernel_selected, kernel_fallback, kernel_latency_hist by kernel_id and device_type. alert rule: kernel_fallback_rate > 0.01 for 5m -> pager to eng-runtime.

mike_g: one more thing — users running private deployments might want to override selection (force A100 path even on H100 for reproducibility). add override in model config: kernel_hint: [force=A100].

jia: good. also add env var REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 for verbose selection logs (only in debug builds) — useful for customer debug sessions.

anika: action items:
- (anika) draft shim API + tests
- (mike_g) write cheap probe snippet and reg pressure notes
- (jia) add quant/profile gating rules and canary config
- (ravi) dashboard + alert queries
- (infra) schedule canary and collect perf traces

mike_g: i'll push a WIP later today. thanks.

anika: thanks all — i'll post PR and ping for quick review. :thumbsup:
